steps.title: Sources in, one SD card image out
steps.body: Two upstream trees (U-Boot and Linux), one file generated by Vivado for this board and one root filesystem go in. One pinned 32-bit Arm compiler builds the first three. Every artifact lands in `build/deploy/`, and `image.sh` assembles the card without root rights.

steps.title: U-Boot is both the first stage and the bootloader
steps.body: A single checkout at a pinned commit and one defconfig, `xilinx_zynq_virt_defconfig`, produce two binaries: the SPL (first stage) and U-Boot proper. Mainline already has everything except this board.

steps.title: The one input that is not a software project
steps.body: Register values for the clocks, DDR and MIO pins, generated by Vivado from the board's hardware design. The build downloads a pinned copy (sha256-checked) or takes your own with `PS7_INIT_SRC`. It is not committed to this repository.

steps.title: One device tree, two consumers
steps.body: U-Boot and Linux each need a device tree for the board and mainline has none for the Eclypse Z7. The same file in `custom/dts/` is copied into both source trees, and a one-line patch per tree adds it to the Makefile.

steps.title: Step 1: prepare the PS7 files, then one make
steps.body: `uboot` extracts and fixes the two ps7 files, merges `config/uboot/eclypse-z7.config` plus a generated line `CONFIG_XILINX_PS_INIT_FILE=...` into the defconfig, and runs one `make` that builds the SPL, `spl/boot.bin` and `u-boot.img`.

steps.title: BOOT.BIN is the SPL in a Zynq boot image
steps.body: 131,676 bytes: a 2,240-byte header written by `mkimage -T zynqimage` followed by the SPL. This is the file the BootROM looks for.

steps.title: Step 2: the kernel from the generic ARMv7 defconfig
steps.body: `multi_v7_defconfig` covers Zynq (`ARCH_ZYNQ=y`), plus a small fragment. The script checks that the options the boot path needs are built in (SD controller, UART console, ext4, MBR parsing) and fails early if not.

steps.title: Step 3: a 32-bit userland
steps.body: Debian trixie for `armhf` via mmdebstrap, or the Alpine `armv7` minirootfs. Building Debian needs qemu-user on every PC, including an ARM64 one: most 64-bit Arm chips cannot run 32-bit code.

steps.title: Step 4: assemble the card, rootless
steps.body: `mke2fs -d` inside `fakeroot` makes the ext4 root, `mkfs.vfat` and `mcopy` fill the FAT partition, `sfdisk` writes the MBR table on a plain file and `dd` places both filesystems. Nothing needs `sudo`.

steps.title: Flash it with the guarded script
steps.body: `./build.sh flash -d /dev/sdX` refuses system disks, shows the card and asks first. `--firmware-only` replaces just `BOOT.BIN` and `u-boot.img`; `--kernel-only` just the kernel, DTB and modules.
